subject.title: Feature: Trigger model fallback on context length exceeded

question: Should OpenClaw allow model fallback after context overflow recovery is exhausted, and under what replay-safety and context-window constraints?
rationale: Both choices are product-valid: current docs and code intentionally keep overflow inside compaction/retry, while the issue reports a real long-session recovery gap that crosses provider routing, replay safety, and context-window semantics.

options.title: Implement Guarded Larger-Window Fallback
options.body: Allow fallback only after compaction and truncation fail, only to candidates with known sufficient effective context, and preserve replay-safety and delivery guards.

options.title: Keep Compaction-Only Behavior
options.body: Document that context overflow is not a model-fallback trigger and improve the user-facing recovery guidance instead.

options.title: Defer To Narrower UX Work
options.body: Prioritize diagnostics and model-switch recovery items while leaving larger-context fallback as an explicit future policy decision.

recommendation.title: Implement Guarded Larger-Window Fallback
recommendation.body: Allow fallback only after compaction and truncation fail, only to candidates with known sufficient effective context, and preserve replay-safety and delivery guards.

likelyOwner.reason: He has current-main history on the affected files and previously framed this issue as a policy choice.
